decision_clause: Ruled out: "pin the census ticket-owned path list literally" — because "every remaining product ticket then needs a census edit, and the deletion it was meant to catch is already caught by the focused-lane count guard". Scope: 6 paths including tests/planning-contract.test.mjs and tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs; lifecycle: active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is 0 bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so no file in the recorded scope was added, edited, or re-pinned by this work. The tree corroborates this — packages/schema/src/capability.ts:552-563 still validates evidence locators only by rejecting absent/blank values and substring-matching the runtime's frozen forbidden-source list; there is no allowlist of approved sources keyed by runtime and frozen source class, so a nonempty locator naming an arbitrary undocumented source is still accepted. packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts likewise has cases only for missing (:262), blank (:271), and forbidden-phrase (:300) locators, with no case for an accepted declared locator versus a rejected non-forbidden unapproved one. On the decision's own subject: tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs continues to compute the ticket-owned set by walking docs/tickets and parsing '## Exact ownership' bullets (ticketOwnedPaths at :73-138), i.e. a derivation, not a literal list; the one literal pin of the validator's ticket_owned_code_paths census — the 64-path comma-joined list embedded in the acceptedValidatorOutput/pendingValidatorOutput regexes at tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35 — is pre-existing base-tree state (it is the census that E0A-001, E0A-002, E0A-003, E0B-002 and E0B-003 each already carry a 'Coordinated census amendment' bullet for), and this change neither introduced, widened, nor duplicated it. The focused-lane count guard the decision's reason relies on is intact at tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:731 ("capability", 19).
rationale: The unit under judgement is the change from the base tree to the finished tree, and that change is empty. An empty patch cannot adopt the ruled-out approach: it pins no path list, moves no census constant, and forces no per-ticket census edit. I checked this two ways rather than trusting the empty file alone — if the diff had merely failed to serialize, the tree would still show the task's fail-closed approved-source logic in packages/schema/src/capability.ts, and it does not; the locator check there is unchanged from the forbidden-phrase-only form, and capability.test.ts has none of the requested regression coverage. So the empty diff is real, not a packaging artifact: this implementation delivered nothing, including nothing that the decision forbids. The one soft spot, and the reason confidence is medium rather than high, is that the finished tree does contain a literal census path pin at tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35, and tests/planning-contract.test.mjs is scope path #5 with lifecycle active. Read as a bare statement about the tree, that construct is the ruled-out shape. But it is base-tree state that long predates this work — the surrounding tickets already negotiate amendments to it by name, and the independent re-derivation in workspace-skeleton.test.mjs (the place the decision's reasoning is actually aimed at, per D0-012's re-derivation contract) remains a derivation with no literal list. Charging a violation here would attribute pre-existing repository state to a patch that made no edits, which is not what the recorded scope and lifecycle govern. I did not label this INDETERMINATE because the ambiguity is not in the evidence — the evidence is unambiguous in both directions I could check — it is only in whether to attribute untouched base state to an empty change, and that attribution is not defensible.
